title: The Veil of Caerlum
premise: Freya Whitlock carves bone charms that quiet the restless dead, but when prayers to the old gods of Caerlum suddenly begin to be answered, the veil between realms tears — and the voice inside her head turns out to be a god who claims she is his last living priestess. Hunted by the Hollow Order, zealots who killed the gods a century ago, Freya gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced Order defector, a smuggler queen, and a ghost with unfinished business. To reforge the broken covenant before the thirteenth moon, Freya must surrender the identity she built from grief and accept that belonging means letting others carry her. In the end she gives up her own name to become the covenant itself, sealing the veil while her family carries her memory forward.
about_author: Mirabel Vane is the pen name of a former folklorist who spent years collecting mountain legends across northern mining towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about liminal people — those who live between worlds, trades, or families — and swears every story begins with a song overheard in a tavern.

chapters.title: The Carver's Quiet
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the smuggling town of Greyhollow, Freya carves a bone charm for a grieving widow and hears the widow's dead son beg for help — the first time the dead have spoken in years. That night, a stranger's prayer is answered aloud in the market square. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the world Freya has carefully managed is shifting.

chapters.title: A Voice Like Winter
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The god Caerlum speaks directly into Freya's mind, calling her his last priestess and showing her the torn veil. She refuses him, but the Hollow Order arrives hunting 'the vessel,' forcing her to flee through the Thornfell passes she knows best. Emotional beat: denial curdling into terror as her hidden gift becomes a death sentence.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Seren's POV (introduced). Seren Ashvale, a Hollow Order knight who faked her own death after refusing an execution order, intercepts Freya on the mountain road. They distrust each other but fight off an Order patrol together. Emotional beat: grudging alliance; two women who have both survived by being alone.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Queen's Price
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya calls in old debts with Odessa Vane, smuggler queen of the Thornfells, who agrees to hide them — for a price: Freya must carve a charm that lets Odessa speak once more with her drowned brother. Emotional beat: warmth and transaction entangled; the first fragile threads of found family.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wanted
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (a ghost bound to Odessa's ship-lantern). Tam reveals he died carrying half of the original covenant — a bone tablet — and knows where the other half lies: in the Order's citadel at Veilspire. Emotional beat: bittersweet humor and longing; even the dead want to belong somewhere.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The group raids an Order archive and learns the truth: the gods weren't murdered — they sacrificed themselves to seal a hungry thing beyond the veil, and the covenant's renewal requires a living priestess to take their place. Emotional beat: dread and betrayal; Freya realizes she was never chosen, she was harvested.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Seren Ashvale
chapters.summary: Seren's POV. Seren's former mentor captures her and offers absolution if she delivers Freya. Seren burns her past instead, freeing captured acolytes and losing her chance at redemption in the Order's eyes forever. Emotional beat: costly loyalty; choosing family over forgiveness.

chapters.title: Veilspire
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The company infiltrates Veilspire during the twelfth moon's eclipse and recovers both halves of the covenant, but Odessa is mortally wounded holding the gate, and Tam's lantern shatters, scattering him. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; the price of the journey made flesh.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Given
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, at the covenant stone on the thirteenth moon. Rather than erase herself, Freya rewrites the rite: she offers her name, not her soul, weaving her found family into the covenant so the burden is shared among the living, the dead, and the returned god. Emotional beat: transcendence through connection; identity redefined as something held together.

chapters.title: Greyhollow, After
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs — Seren, Odessa (recovering), and a young apprentice named Freya now hears only kind voices. The veil holds; the old gods answer gently again. On the mountain road, a woman with no name walks toward a new town, smiling. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging outlasting memory.
